subject: Integration hypothesis & prioritized risks — Redwood SDK / embeddings / structured outputs
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Li <sam.li@sequoia-thera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Integration hypothesis & prioritized risks — Redwood SDK / embeddings / structured outputs

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap to make sure we captured Sequoia's priorities and constraints, plus proposed next actions on our side. If anything below is off, flag it and we'll adjust.

Key pain points you shared:
- Clinical triage summaries often return inconsistent field structure; downstream systems require deterministic JSON for EHR ingest.
- Search/ranking of prior notes returns lots of noise; you want reranking by clinical relevance (not just lexical).
- Latency sensitivity in triage: target 200ms median for single-turn summary paths.
- PHI/regulatory: prefer VPC or on-prem with customer-managed keys; SOC 2 evidence required.

Our high-level integration hypothesis:
- Use Redwood Private (VPC) with a dedicated small GPU pool for the triage/summary route.
- Surface a streaming + function-calling path in the Redwood SDK so the model returns structured JSON increments (streamed chunks) that are validated client-side before EHR ingestion.
- Embed + rerank pipeline: generate 1536-d embeddings, index with FAISS (dense search), then run a lightweight reranker model (lower-cost Redwood variant) to improve top-K relevance.
- Latency plan: enable request-level prefix/KV caching for repeated patient prompts, and tune batching to keep median under 200ms for single-user flows.
- Security: VPC peering + KMS integration, audit-log retention 1 year minimum for the POC; SOC 2 package attached.

Proposed prioritization (owners & rough ETA):
1) Technical POC scope doc + sample SDK snippet (Redwood) — Priya / Ben — by 2026-10-02
2) Network & security checklist + KMS details for legal / security review — Grace — by 2026-10-04
3) Mutual action plan (timeline + success metrics) — shared XLS attached — Priya — by 2026-10-05
4) Procurement signals / MSA draft — Sequoia procurement + our RevOps — initiate week of 2026-10-06

Attachments: sequoia_SOC2_questions.pdf (your questionnaire), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (our draft timeline), redwood_integration_sketch.png (high-level topology).

Questions for you now:
- Confirm that deterministic JSON is strictly required (field order/typing) or if schema-validation at ingest layer is sufficient.
- Do you prefer the POC to run in your VPC (preferred) or Redwood-hosted but isolated environment?

I can circulate a 1-page POC scope + small SDK snippet demonstrating streaming + funcall-style structured output within 24 hours if you want that before the network/security work.

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0142

Attachment(s): sequoia_SOC2_questions.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx, redwood_integration_sketch.png

From: Sam Li <sam.li@sequoia-thera.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sequoia-thera.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 17:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration hypothesis & prioritized risks — Redwood SDK / embeddings / structured outputs

Priya —

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches what came out of the call. A few clarifications and asks from our side:

1) Deterministic structured output: we need a predictable JSON schema (field names + types). Field order isn't strictly enforced, but typing and presence of required fields is mandatory.

2) Tech stack: Node (TypeScript) services deployed in AWS ECS today. We can run the POC either in our VPC or accept a tightly isolated Redwood-hosted environment if you can guarantee no PHI persistence and provide audit logs.

3) Latency target: 200ms median for single-turn summaries is a hard requirement for this workflow. If streaming incurs noticeable end-to-end latency overhead we may need to trade off chunk size vs latency. Please include streaming latency estimates in the POC.

4) Procurement: attached is our SOC questionnaire (filled partially) and procurement@ is looped for MSA timing. We generally prefer a short pilot agreement before broad MSA signatures.

Next steps we expect from Redwood: POC scope + sample SDK snippet demonstrating streaming + funcall-like structured output, and a one-page security checklist for our InfoSec.

Would appreciate a POC window the week of Oct 4 or Oct 11.

Thanks,

Sam Li
Head of Clinical Platforms
Sequoia Therapeutics
sam.li@sequoia-thera.com

Attachment(s): sequoia_SOC2_questions-answered.pdf

Ben / Priya —

This is great and addresses our main concerns. The TypeScript snippet is exactly what our engineers wanted to see. We can confirm:
- Deterministic schema validation at ingest is sufficient.
- We will aim to host the POC in our VPC and provide the network details next week.
- Oct 6 works for a kick-off call to start the POC; procurement will aim to issue a short pilot order within the same week.

Please send the POC scope + sample SDK repo link by Friday 2026-10-02.
